problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `5000` nodes
- `-5000 <= Node.val <= 5000`
problems.statement:
Reverse a singly linked list by rewiring its `next` pointers, and return the new head.

The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail. Can you do it both iteratively and recursively?
problems.title: Reverse Linked List

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `1` and `5 * 10^4` nodes
- `1 <= Node.val <= 1000`
problems.statement:
A list `L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln-1 -> Ln` must be rearranged **in place** into
`L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> Ln-2 -> ...`, alternating from the front and the back.

Rewire the nodes themselves (don't just change their values) and return the head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Reorder List

problems.constraints:
- the list has `n` nodes, `1 <= k <= n <= 5000`
- `0 <= Node.val <= 1000`
problems.statement:
Split the list into consecutive groups of `k` nodes and reverse the nodes inside each full group. If the
last group has fewer than `k` nodes, leave it as it is.

Rewire the nodes (don't only swap values) and return the new head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.

Can you use only `O(1)` extra memory?
problems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group

tests.explanation: Groups [1,2] and [3,4] flip; 5 is left alone.

problems.constraints:
- the list has `n` nodes, `1 <= n <= 500`
- `-500 <= Node.val <= 500`
- `1 <= left <= right <= n`
problems.statement:
Given the head of a list and positions `left <= right` (1-based), reverse the nodes from position `left`
through position `right` and return the head. The rest of the list keeps its order. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.

Can you do it in a single pass?
problems.title: Reverse Linked List II

problems.constraints:
- the list has `n` nodes, `1 <= k <= n <= 10^5`
- `0 <= Node.val <= 100`
problems.statement:
Given the head of a list and an integer `k`, swap the **values** of the `k`-th node from the beginning
and the `k`-th node from the end (both 1-based), and return the head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `1` and `10^5` nodes
- `0 <= Node.val <= 10^5`
problems.statement:
Split the list into consecutive groups whose intended sizes are `1, 2, 3, 4, ...`. The last group may be
shorter than intended if the list runs out of nodes.

Reverse the nodes of every group whose **actual** length is even, and return the head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Reverse Nodes In Even Length Groups

tests.explanation: The groups are [1], [1,0] and [6]; only [1,0] is reversed.
The last group [6,5] has even length and is reversed.

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `100` nodes
- `0 <= Node.val <= 100`
problems.statement:
Swap every two adjacent nodes of the list and return the new head. Rewire the nodes; don't change the
values stored in them. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs

tests.explanation: The odd node at the end stays.

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `1000` nodes
- `0 <= Node.val <= 1000`
- `1 <= k <= 50`
problems.statement:
Split the list into `k` consecutive parts whose lengths differ by at most one, with longer parts first.
Some parts may be empty when the list has fewer than `k` nodes.

Return the `k` part heads in order (an empty part is `null`, shown as `[]`). The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Split Linked List in Parts

tests.explanation: Three parts of one node, then two empty parts.

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `10^4` nodes
- `1 <= Node.val <= 50`
- `0 <= val <= 50`
problems.statement: Remove every node whose value equals `val` and return the new head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Remove Linked List Elements

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `1` and `10^4` nodes
- `1 <= Node.val <= 10^6`
- `1 <= m, n <= 1000`
problems.statement:
Walk through the list repeating this pattern until the end: **keep** the next `m` nodes, then **delete**
the following `n` nodes (or as many as remain). Return the head of the modified list. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Delete N Nodes After M Nodes of a Linked List

tests.explanation: Keep 1,2, drop 3,4,5, keep 6,7, drop 8,9,10, keep 11,12, drop 13.

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `300` nodes
- `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`
- the list is sorted in ascending order
problems.statement:
The list is sorted. Delete nodes so that each value appears only once, and return the head of the
(still sorted) list. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `5 * 10^4` nodes
- `-10^6 <= Node.val, insertVal <= 10^6`
problems.statement:
You are given one node, `head`, of a **circular** linked list whose values are sorted in non-decreasing
order when read around the circle starting from the smallest value. `head` itself may be any node of the
circle, not necessarily the smallest.

Insert a new node with value `insertVal` so that the circle stays sorted, and return `head`. If several
places work, any of them is accepted. If the list is empty (`head` is `null`), create a one-node circular
list and return that node.

**How the tests describe the list:** the values are listed once, starting from `head`; the judge links
the last node back to the first. Your answer is shown as one lap of values starting from the returned node.
problems.title: Insert into a Sorted Circular Linked List

tests.explanation: 2 goes between 1 and 3: one lap from head is 3, 4, 1, 2.
An empty list becomes a single node pointing to itself.
With a single node, 0 goes right after it.

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `10^4` nodes
- `-10^6 <= Node.val <= 10^6`
problems.statement:
Rearrange the list so that all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, ...) come first, followed by all
nodes at even positions, each group keeping its original relative order. Return the head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.

Positions are counted from 1 and have nothing to do with the node values. Use `O(1)` extra space.
problems.title: Odd Even Linked List

problems.constraints:
- the list has between `0` and `500` nodes
- `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`
- `0 <= k <= 2 * 10^9`
problems.statement:
Rotate the list to the right by `k` places: each rotation moves the last node to the front. `k` may be
much larger than the length of the list. Return the new head. The list is given (and your answer is shown) as its values from head to tail.
problems.title: Rotate List

tests.explanation: 4 rotations of a 3-node list equal 1 rotation.
